components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The high-confidence action for sending, saving, or starting work.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M3 8h9M8 4l4 4-4 4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>Send</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #202b3a; color: #fbf8f2; border: 1px solid #202b3a; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 16px; font: 600 14px/20px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; transition: background 200ms ease, border-color 200ms ease, box-shadow 200ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #ad4937; border-color: #ad4937; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ad4937; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: A quiet paper field that gains a rust focus ring when active.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" placeholder="Ask Research Companion…" aria-label="Research message"/>
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: #fbf8f2; color: #202b3a; border: 1px solid #d8cdbd; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 12px; font: 400 14px/20px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #5e6670; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ad4937; outline-offset: 2px; border-color: #ad4937; }

components.name: Evidence Card
components.description: A bordered evidence block that keeps provenance close to the excerpt.
components.css: .ds-evidence { margin: 0; background: #f4efe6; color: #202b3a; border: 1px solid #d8cdbd; border-radius: 8px; padding: 12px; font: 400 14px/24px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-evidence p { margin: 0 0 6px; } .ds-evidence small { color: #5e6670; font: 600 11px/16px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; letter-spacing: .06em; text-transform: uppercase; }

narrative.overview:
Research Companion now feels like a working archive: warm paper, ink-blue structure, and deliberate marks for evidence, attention, and state. The interface is calm enough for sustained reading but has a visible point of view suited to a portfolio artifact about agentic research and persistent memory.

The system uses editorial contrast instead of generic dashboard gray. Serif headings give the product a human, note-taking voice; the body remains a pragmatic system sans for scanability; monospace stays reserved for IDs, timestamps, arguments, and source material. Surfaces are layered tonally with restrained shadows, while rust and brass are reserved for meaningful signals.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper canvas with ink-navy structure.
Rust evidence marks and brass active states.
Editorial serif headings with utilitarian sans body copy.
Rounded, tactile controls with quiet borders.
Evidence and state remain visible without decorative noise.

rules.name: The Evidence Mark Rule
rules.body: Rust and brass should communicate a state or provenance cue; never use them as ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Instrument Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for information that behaves like an instrument reading—not for the whole interface.

rules.name: The Quiet Surface Rule
rules.body: A surface is either separated by a border or a shadow; use both only when the component needs protected focus.

dos: Do use warm paper, ink navy, rust, and brass as functional visual language.
Do reserve monospace for source IDs, arguments, timestamps, and code.
Do make memory provenance and state readable within seconds.
Do keep borders quiet and use one elevation treatment per surface.
donts: Don't bring back the teal/gray dashboard palette.
Don't use gradients, glass, or decorative blur as theme substitutes.
Don't use thick colored side borders for evidence, alerts, or cards.
Don't use accent colors without a state, provenance, or interaction reason.
